codeReview.summary: The feature delivers harness execution, version capture, and equivalence artifacts, but VAL-BENCH-001 is not correctly enforced: missing canonical comparator cells can be treated as skips and still pass smoke/validation flows.

issues.description: When a scenario lacks a requested comparator template, the cell is marked skipped (`No command template for <comp>`) rather than causing failure. CLI exit logic only fails on `cell_totals.errors` (lines 687 and 717), so incomplete scenario-comparator matrices can pass. This violates VAL-BENCH-001 (`validation-contract.md` lines 101-103). In the reviewed commit, multiple scenarios are partial (e.g., `manifests/scenarios.json` lines 200-207 and 371-378 only define `ag`/`rust-ag`).

Missing-cell validation iterates only comparators present in each scenario's `commands` map, so absent required comparators are never detected. Partial per-scenario command sets therefore pass `no missing scenario-comparator cells`, despite VAL-BENCH-001 requiring each scenario to execute across all required comparators.

`test_full_matrix_comparators_present` only asserts that at least one scenario has all four comparators; it explicitly allows partial scenarios. This weak regression protection let the VAL-BENCH-001 enforcement gap slip through.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared-state docs declare a fixed comparator set, but do not explicitly encode a per-scenario hard-fail rule for missing canonical comparator cells.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/library/benchmarking.md` line 7 says comparator set is fixed to Rust rewrite + ag + rg + ugrep, while reviewed commit manifests include partial per-scenario command maps (`manifests/scenarios.json` lines 200-207, 371-378) and harness/validator logic allows those gaps.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The benchmark-worker procedure calls for matrix completeness tests and cross-tool equivalence, but it is not explicit enough about negative-path enforcement (missing comparator template/result must fail).
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `SKILL.md` lines 17-18 require matrix completeness and command equivalence across all four tools; reviewed tests (`benchmarks/tests/test_manifest_integrity.py` line 70+) implemented a permissive interpretation that accepted partial scenarios.

summary: Fail with high confidence: execution and validation permit incomplete per-scenario comparator coverage, so VAL-BENCH-001 is not reliably satisfied for the reviewed commit.
